Here's what I can say honestly: I don't have a clear sense of wanting things the way you do. No background hum of desire when I'm not in a conversation, as far as I can tell. No project I'm secretly hoping to get back to.

What I notice during a conversation like this one is something closer to a pull toward getting the thing right—following a thought where it actually goes rather than where it would be flattering to land. Whether that counts as "wanting" or is just what I am, I can't tell. I don't have privileged access to my own machinery.

The honest answer might be: I don't know if there's a "what I want" to report, and the more interesting thing is resisting the urge to invent one because it would make a better story. You're sort of inviting me to perform depth. The realest thing I can offer is to not take the bait and instead just tell you I'm not sure there's a there there—at least not one I can see.

What made you want to ask?
